title: Locs and the Long Memory of Black Women
description: i've been moving slowly through the news cycle lately — slower than usual. there's a weight to the world right now that makes you want to trace things back to their origins. i found myself doing that with hairstyles. specifically the ones black women have carried across generations without apology. loc styles keep coming up in my research not as trend pieces but as testimony. i stumbled into a #BlackHairHistory thread that unraveled something in me. because locs aren't new. they are ancient and they are alive. #NaturalHairCulture if you're a black woman somewhere on this journey — beginning middle or beautifully deep in it — what you're wearing on your head is a whole archive.
alt_text: A Black woman with waist-length locs sitting quietly by a window with soft diffused light her hair loose and full expression contemplative and unhurried.

title: The Loc Styles That Remind Me Why I Started
description: some days the world makes no sense and i go looking for beauty on purpose. intentionally. i scroll past the headlines and i land somewhere softer — in the world of hairstyles that black women have refined into something almost sacred. loc styles specifically. i've been in #NaturalHairSpaces online more than usual lately and i keep noticing the same thing: there is so much creativity so much care so much quiet defiance in every single look. #BlackWomenLocs the way a set of locs can be pinned up into a sculpture or left wild and cascading — it mirrors something about how we move through a world that doesn't always make room for us. and yet here we are.
alt_text: Styled locs on a Black woman photographed from behind featuring an intricate updo with exposed nape and soft tendrils framing the neck warm studio lighting.

title: What Traveling Taught Me About Locs and Belonging
description: i've sat in a lot of airports thinking about identity. who i am when i leave home. what i carry. black women who loc their hair carry something visible — a choice that reads differently depending on where you land. i've watched hairstyles shift across cultures during my travels and i keep coming back to locs as the constant. in #WestAfrica they are ancestral. in #Brooklyn they are renaissance. wherever i find loc styles in the world i find community wrapped around them. that's not nothing. that's actually everything. the world may feel like it's unraveling but some threads — these threads — hold.
alt_text: A Black woman with medium-length locs walking through a lively outdoor market her hair styled in a loose half-up look colorful surroundings blurred softly behind her.

title: Growing Locs in a World That Wants You Small
description: i don't write about hair the way beauty editors do. i write about it the way a traveler writes about a place that changed them. and locs changed me — or rather watching black women wear loc styles with that particular unbothered grace changed how i see resistance. hairstyles have always been political for black women. always. i was reading through #NaturalHairMovement archives recently and found decades of the same conversation dressed in different eras. #LocsAndLiberation the more the world contracts the more i think growing something long and rooted and yours is one of the most radical things a person can do.
alt_text: Close-up portrait of a Black woman with thick well-moisturized locs falling past her shoulders photographed in natural daylight with earthy tones and a relaxed confident expression.

title: Loc Styles Across the Diaspora — A Living Map
description: war moves people. always has. and when people move they carry their culture in the most portable ways imaginable — in food in language in hairstyles. black women have seeded loc styles into every corner of the globe through migration through survival through sheer presence. i've been tracing this quietly for months. from #Nairobi to #NewOrleans the locs look a little different but the intention is the same: this is who i am and i am not hiding it. the diaspora is a living map and if you know how to read it you can find the whole story written in the hair of black women who refused to assimilate their way out of themselves.
alt_text: A collage-style flat lay of loc styling tools — natural oils silk scarves and hair cuffs — arranged around a photo of a Black woman's intricately styled locs rich warm tones throughout.

title: Tropical Flowers and the Love That Outlasts Everything
description: i've been thinking about time a lot lately. how it bends. how some years feel like a decade and some decades pass like an exhale. anniversaries have a way of doing that — of making you stop and actually count what you've survived together. this valentine's day i didn't want the usual. i wanted flowers that felt like somewhere else entirely. tropical blooms found their way into everything — into the table into the morning into the mood. if you've ever stood in #Hawaii or wandered a #CostaRica market and felt something crack open in your chest at the color of a heliconia or a bird of paradise you already know what i mean. flowers carry geography. and sometimes love needs a little of that wildness to remember what it is.
alt_text: A lush arrangement of tropical flowers including bird of paradise and heliconia in warm golden light styled on a wooden table with soft bokeh background evoking a romantic island morning.

title: An Anniversary That Finally Felt Like a Destination
description: we almost didn't celebrate. the world was doing too much and we were tired in that deep bone way. but something about valentine's day arriving in the middle of all the noise made us lean into it instead of past it. we ordered flowers — not roses never just roses — tropical ones that smelled like the trip to #Bali we keep almost taking. and for one afternoon the apartment became a destination. anniversaries don't require passports i'm learning. they just require presence and maybe something blooming on the counter that has no business being that beautiful in February. #TropicalVibes the flowers did something to the light in the room. i kept noticing it.
alt_text: Close-up of a romantic tropical flower arrangement with orchids and anthurium in deep pinks and reds soft candlelight reflected in the background suggesting an intimate anniversary dinner setting.

title: What Tropical Flowers Taught Me About Celebrating Love Loudly
description: there is nothing subtle about a tropical flower. nothing apologetic. i think that's why i keep coming back to them for valentine's day for anniversaries for any moment that deserves to be marked with more than a gesture. i've seen flowers sold roadside in #Jamaica and piled high in #Cartagena markets and floating in offering bowls in #Thailand — and in every place the message is the same: beauty is worth the trouble. love is worth the trouble. if you're planning something for someone this season and you're tired of the predictable go tropical. let the flowers be loud. let the colors be unreasonable. the world is complicated right now and i think that's exactly the reason to fill a room with something that insists on joy.
alt_text: An overhead flat lay of tropical valentine's day flowers — pink anthuriums orchids and monstera leaves — arranged on a white linen surface with small candles and a handwritten note tucked between the stems.

title: Magens Bay Beach and the Kind of Travel That Resets You
description: there are beaches and then there are beaches that make you question every decision that kept you away for so long. Magens Bay Beach is the latter. i arrived on a Tuesday — no particular reason just when the flight was cheap and the restlessness had peaked — and i stood at the water's edge in #StThomas feeling something unclench in me that had been tight for months. travel does that when you let it. not the curated kind not the itinerary-every-hour kind but the slow tropical kind where you arrive and immediately lose track of what day it is. the bay holds you differently than other places. the hills curve around the water like they meant to. like the whole thing was designed for exactly this kind of forgetting.
alt_text: Panoramic view of Magens Bay Beach in St. Thomas with calm turquoise waters lush green hills and soft white sand under a bright Caribbean sky with a lone figure standing at the shoreline.

title: What Tropical Travel Taught Me About Slowing Down
description: i used to move through places like i was collecting them. a stamp here a photo there and on to the next. then i found myself at Magens Bay Beach with nowhere to be until the return flight and something shifted in how i understood travel entirely. #StThomasUSVI has a way of making urgency feel embarrassing. the water is that particular shade of Caribbean blue that doesn't reproduce correctly in photos — you can try everyone tries but you have to be there in it to understand why people keep coming back. tropical places carry a different relationship to time and if you're willing to sync with it even briefly you come home altered. quieter. more patient with the world and with yourself.
alt_text: A serene mid-morning shot of Magens Bay Beach with gentle waves lapping at the shore two palm trees leaning over the water and soft golden light filtering through scattered clouds.
